sentences.text: Fluvionectes translates to river swimmer, combining Latin and Greek roots.
The defining specimen was likely a young adult measuring between 5 and 5.2 meters long and weighing 392 kilograms.
A larger, more mature individual suggests the animal may have reached a maximum body length of 7 meters.
The skeleton contained 76 gastroliths, mostly disc-shaped stones made of black chert and grey quartzite.
Coalified wood found with the remains suggests the animal died after being caught in a log jam.
This genus is known from a single holotype specimen that includes parts of the trunk region.
Fluvionectes is classified in the family Elasmosauridae and the subfamily Elasmosaurinae, sharing a clade with Albertonectes, Nakonanectes, Styxosaurus, and Terminonatator.
Fluvionectes appears to have lived in freshwater and brackish water environments, unlike most other elasmosaurs which were oceanic.
Fluvionectes lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
